title: Distance Metrics
text: core stGradient analyzing genomic features change function distance tumor boundaries. vignette covers boundary distance calculation, available separation metrics, run distance profile analysis.

title: Distance Metrics
text: defining regions (see Region Selection), compute signed distances cell nearest polygon boundary: Distances signed: Negative values = cells inside polygon (tumor) Positive values = cells outside polygon (stroma/microenvironment)
code: library(stGradient)  seurat_obj$boundary_distance <- calculate_boundary_distances(seurat_obj, auto_polygons)

title: Distance Metrics
text: stGradient computes three complementary separation metrics:

title: Distance Metrics
text: Measures overall gene expression dissimilarity cell groups (1 - Pearson correlation mean expression profiles). Range: 0 (identical) 2 (anti-correlated) Higher values = greater expression differences
code: td <- calculate_transcriptomic_distance(inside_cells, outside_cells, seurat_obj)

title: Distance Metrics
text: Sum squared differences cell type proportions inside outside groups. Range: 0 (identical composition) ~2 Independent sample size
code: cd <- calculate_composition_difference(inside_cells, outside_cells, seurat_obj, group_by = "cellType")

title: Distance Metrics
text: Mean absolute log2 fold-change top 100 DE genes groups. Higher values = stronger transcriptional changes boundary
code: de <- calculate_de_strength(inside_cells, outside_cells, seurat_obj)

title: Distance Metrics
text: main analysis function calculates metrics across range distances:
code: results <- calculate_distance_profile(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   distance_thresholds = seq(10, 200, by = 10),   metric = "all",   group_by = "cellType",   inside_mode = "all" )  distance_profile <- results$profile celltype_contributions <- results$celltype_contributions

title: Distance Metrics
text: stGradient supports two modes defining “inside” cell group:
code: # Compare both modes results_all <- calculate_distance_profile(seurat_obj, inside_mode = "all") results_dist <- calculate_distance_profile(seurat_obj, inside_mode = "distance")  combined <- rbind(results_all$profile, results_dist$profile)

title: Distance Metrics
text: Identify distance separation maximized:
code: critical <- find_critical_distance(distance_profile, "transcriptomic_distance")  cat("Maximum separation at:", critical$max_distance, "μm\n") cat("Plateau begins at:", critical$plateau_distance, "μm\n")

title: Distance Metrics
code: # Compare inside modes plot_distance_comparison(combined)  # All metrics faceted plot_all_metrics(combined)  # Cell type contribution heatmap plot_celltype_heatmap(celltype_contributions)  # Proportion trajectories for top cell types plot_celltype_proportions(celltype_contributions, top_n = 5)

title: Gene-Distance Analysis
text: stGradient provides tools model individual gene expression function distance tumor boundaries T-cell hotspots. identifies genes whose expression systematically increases decreases distance key spatial landmarks.

title: Gene-Distance Analysis
text: First, compute per-cell signed distance using concave hull boundary: adds dist_to_boundary abs_dist_to_boundary metadata columns. Negative values indicate intratumoral cells, positive values indicate peritumoral/stromal cells.
code: library(stGradient)  seurat_obj <- compute_distance_from_boundary(   seurat_obj,   polygon_col = "inside_polygon",   intratumoral_label = TRUE,   fov_name = "fov",   concavity = 2 )

title: Gene-Distance Analysis
text: Fit per-gene linear models Spearman correlations:
code: dist_res <- find_distance_associated_genes(   seurat_obj,   assay = "Xenium",   focus = "peritumoral",   min_cells_expressing = 10,   n_distance_bins = 10,   max_dist_quantile = 0.95,   p_adj_threshold = 0.05 )

title: Gene-Distance Analysis
code: dist_plots <- plot_distance_genes(dist_res, top_n = 12, sample_label = "Sample_01")  # Volcano plot of gene significance dist_plots$volcano  # Expression trends for top genes across distance bins dist_plots$trends

title: Gene-Distance Analysis
code: plot_tcell_hotspots(seurat_obj, hs, celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas")

title: Loading & Setup

title: Niche Analysis
text: stGradient includes complete niche analysis workflow comparing spatial neighborhood composition clinical groups (e.g., pCR vs non-pCR neoadjuvant chemotherapy studies). pipeline identifies cellular niches, quantifies patient-level proportions, tests associations outcome.

title: Niche Analysis
text: workflow proceeds three steps: Build niches — compute per-cell k-nearest-neighbor neighborhoods cluster Test associations — Wilcoxon/permutation tests logistic regression Visualize results — composition plots, bar charts, coefficient plots

title: Niche Analysis
text: run_niche_pipeline() function operates list Seurat objects (one per patient/sample):
code: library(stGradient)  # Define clinical status table pcr_status <- data.frame(   patient_id = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "P4"),   pCR = c(1L, 1L, 0L, 0L) )  # Use a stable set of cell types across all samples all_celltypes <- c("Cancer LumA SC", "T Cells CD4+", "T Cells CD8+",                    "Macrophages", "Fibroblasts", "Endothelial")  # Intratumoral niches (cells inside polygons) intra <- run_niche_pipeline(   seurat_list = seurat_list,   subset_value = TRUE,   pcr_status = pcr_status,   all_celltypes = all_celltypes,   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas",   polygon_col = "inside_polygon",   k = 20,   n_niches = 8 )  # Peritumoral niches (cells outside polygons) peri <- run_niche_pipeline(   seurat_list = seurat_list,   subset_value = FALSE,   pcr_status = pcr_status,   all_celltypes = all_celltypes )

title: Niche Analysis
text: subset_value — TRUE intratumoral, FALSE peritumoral k — number nearest neighbors neighborhood computation n_niches — number niche clusters identify

title: Niche Analysis
text: run_niche_pipeline() returns list : - niche_prop_df — patient × niche proportion data frame (patient_id pCR columns) - niche_composition — cell type composition niche

title: Niche Analysis
text: Returns data frame Wilcoxon p-values permutation-based p-values niche.
code: intra_niches <- setdiff(colnames(intra$niche_prop_df), c("patient_id", "pCR")) intra_X <- as.matrix(intra$niche_prop_df[, intra_niches, drop = FALSE]) intra_y <- intra$niche_prop_df$pCR  stat_intra <- run_niche_stat_tests(intra_X, intra_y, intra_niches, n_perm = 1000)

title: Niche Analysis
text: Fits one logistic regression per niche (proportion → pCR status) returns coefficients, standard errors, p-values.
code: lr_intra <- run_niche_univariate_lr(intra_X, intra_y, intra_niches)

title: Niche Analysis
text: Per-patient niche proportion stacked bar charts, grouped pCR status:
code: plot_niche_stacked_composition(intra$niche_prop_df)

title: Niche Analysis
text: Side--side mean proportions pCR vs non-pCR error bars:
code: plot_niche_grouped_bars(   stat_intra, intra_X, intra_y, intra_niches,   title = "Intratumoral Niches" )

title: Niche Analysis
text: Forest plot log-odds coefficients confidence intervals:
code: plot_niche_coefficients(lr_intra, title = "Intratumoral Niches")

title: Niche Analysis
text: common workflow compares intratumoral peritumoral niches:
code: # Run both compartments intra <- run_niche_pipeline(seurat_list, subset_value = TRUE, pcr_status = pcr_status,                             all_celltypes = all_celltypes) peri <- run_niche_pipeline(seurat_list, subset_value = FALSE, pcr_status = pcr_status,                            all_celltypes = all_celltypes)  # Test both stat_intra <- run_niche_stat_tests(intra_X, intra_y, intra_niches) stat_peri <- run_niche_stat_tests(peri_X, peri_y, peri_niches)

title: PCF Analysis
text: stGradient includes optimized helpers spatstat-based Pair Correlation Function (PCF) analysis. functions specifically analyze spatial co-occurrence cell types outside tumor polygons, characterizing peritumoral microenvironment architecture.

title: PCF Analysis
text: PCF analysis requires spatstat.geom spatstat.explore packages: also need Seurat object polygons defined (see Region Selection).
code: install.packages(c("spatstat.geom", "spatstat.explore"))

title: PCF Analysis
text: Calculate cross-type PCF values specific target distance:
code: library(stGradient)  pcf_summary <- calculate_pcf_outside_summary(    seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   polygons = auto_polygons,   distance = 200,   min_cells = 10,   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas",   include_self_pairs = TRUE,   ordered_pairs = FALSE )

title: PCF Analysis
text: distance — target radius (microns) evaluate PCF min_cells — minimum cells per cell type include analysis include_self_pairs — whether compute -type PCF (e.g., -) ordered_pairs — FALSE computes pair (-B); TRUE computes (-B B-)

title: PCF Analysis
text: Visualize pairwise PCF values heatmap:  midpoint 1 represents complete spatial randomness, warm colors indicating co-occurrence cool colors indicating avoidance.
code: plot_pcf_outside_heatmap(pcf_summary, midpoint = 1)

title: PCF Analysis
text: Generate Monte Carlo envelope curves cell-type pairs assess statistical significance: creates multi-page PDF one page per cell-type pair showing observed PCF simulation envelopes. Points outside envelope represent statistically significant spatial patterns.
code: env_list <- plot_pcf_outside_pair_envelopes(   seurat_obj = seurat_obj,   polygons = auto_polygons,   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas",   min_cells = 10,   include_self_pairs = FALSE,   ordered_pairs = FALSE,   nsim = 39,   bw = 10,   file = "pcf_outside_all_pairs.pdf" )

title: PCF Analysis
text: focused analysis specific cell-type pairs:
code: plot_pcf_pair_gg(env_list[["TypeA_vs_TypeB"]])

title: Region Selection
text: stGradient provides two approaches defining tumor regions: Interactive selection via Shiny app Automated detection using DBSCAN clustering

title: Region Selection
text: Shiny app allows interactively draw polygons spatial data define tumor regions:
code: launch_stGradient()

title: Region Selection
text: Enter Seurat object name — name object R session Enter FOV name — field view name (typically "fov") Click “Load Data” — loads cell coordinates plots Draw polygons — use freehand drawing toolbar plot Enter polygon object name — name extracted polygon object Click “Extract Polygons” — saves polygons global environment resulting polygon object sf object can passed directly downstream stGradient functions.

title: Region Selection
text: add_dbscan_polygons() function automatically identifies tumor regions clustering cancer-labeled cells using DBSCAN algorithm, wrapping detected clusters concave hull polygons.
code: library(stGradient)  # One-step: detect polygons and add membership to Seurat object seurat_obj <- add_dbscan_polygons(seurat_obj)  # Access the polygon object auto_polygons <- seurat_obj@images[["fov"]]@boundaries$cancer_regions

title: Region Selection
text: can tune clustering behavior:
code: seurat_obj <- add_dbscan_polygons(   seurat_obj,   eps = 35,         # neighborhood radius (microns)   minPts = 20,      # minimum cluster size   concavity = 2     # concave hull tightness (lower = tighter) )

title: Region Selection
text: Use plot_dbscan_polygons() inspect results proceeding:
code: # Plot with polygons overlaid plot_dbscan_polygons(seurat_obj)  # Get polygons without plotting (useful for pipelines) auto_polygons <- plot_dbscan_polygons(seurat_obj, plot = FALSE)

title: Region Selection
text: ’re unsure eps minPts values work best data, use optimize_dbscan_params() perform grid search evaluated silhouette score: can customize search ranges:
code: # Search over a grid of eps and minPts values results <- optimize_dbscan_params(seurat_obj)  # View top parameter combinations head(results)  # Use the best parameters best <- results[1, ] seurat_obj <- add_dbscan_polygons(seurat_obj, eps = best$eps, minPts = best$minPts) results <- optimize_dbscan_params(   seurat_obj,   eps_range = seq(20, 80, by = 10),   minPts_range = c(15, 20, 30, 50),   max_sample = 30000  # reduce for faster computation )

title: Region Selection
text: polygons (either Shiny app DBSCAN), annotate cell inside outside: adds inside_polygon column seurat_obj@meta.data logical values.
code: # Add inside/outside metadata column seurat_obj <- add_polygon_membership(seurat_obj, auto_polygons)

title: Region Selection
text: assigning membership, use qc_plot_xenium() visualize spatial layout:
code: qc_out <- qc_plot_xenium(   obj = seurat_obj,   roi_col = "inside_polygon",   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas",   show = "both",   zoom = TRUE,   zoom_pad = 0.05,   grey_outside_roi = TRUE )  qc_out$p

title: Region Selection
text: Examine cell type distributions inside vs. outside region:
code: # Distribution inside ROI only plot_roi_celltype_dist(   df = qc_out$df,   roi_col = "inside_polygon",   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas",   metric = "proportion" ) # Stacked inside vs outside plot_roi_inout_celltype_stack(   df = qc_out$df,   roi_col = "inside_polygon",   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas" ) #Dodged inside vs outside plot_roi_inout_celltype_dodge(   df = qc_out$df,   roi_col = "inside_polygon",   celltype_col = "singleR.predicted.id.brcaAtlas",   metric = "count",   top_n = 10 )
